findings.title: Single-droplet, single-instance runtime is a hard SPOF
evidence: infra/terraform/digitalocean/droplet.tf:1-20 — one digitalocean_droplet.portal resource per environment; no replica set or autoscaling
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:68-184 — exactly one api, one worker, one web container; :27-61 one non-replicated Redis (mem_limit 48m) shared by cache, queue, idempotency and scan locks
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:310-337 — one Caddy ingress; :207-307 one Prometheus + one Alertmanager
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:809-815 — every deploy runs `docker compose down` before `up` (stop-the-world: the portal is offline until the health gate passes, up to ~3 min)
docs/PLATFORM_FAILURE_RUNBOOKS.md:11-13 — runbooks explicitly acknowledge the single point of failure
findings.impact: Loss of the droplet, Redis, or Caddy takes the whole portal offline (web, API, worker, notifications, webhooks) with no failover. Every deploy is a full outage window because the stack is stopped before the new one starts. Hosted Supabase is an external hard dependency with no self-hosted fallback (docs/PLATFORM_FAILURE_RUNBOOKS.md:16-20).
findings.recommendation: Keep the runbooks. Budget a second droplet or at minimum a documented blue/green or `up -d` without `down` deploy path to remove the per-deploy outage; state the availability target and the deploy downtime window in docs/SLO.md. Redis remains a shared SPOF (see the shared-Redis finding).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: platform failure/recovery runbooks present and extended; topology unchanged (single droplet, single instance, single Redis) and the deploy is still stop-the-world — status stays partially-fixed. Owner/budget decision.

findings.title: API defaults to the service-role DB client (RLS bypass)
evidence: apps/api/src/services/supabase.ts:198-226 — getScopedClient returns the user-scoped (RLS) client only when the module is listed in RLS_READS_ENABLED/RLS_WRITES_ENABLED and the request carries a user JWT; otherwise it returns the service-role admin client and records portal_rls_bypass_total
apps/api/src/lib/rls-startup-check.ts:40-46 — production refuses to boot when RLS_READS_ENABLED is empty; :48-53 writes log an error (non-fatal) when RLS_WRITES_ENABLED is empty
apps/api/src/main.ts:12-14 — assertRlsStartupConfig(env) runs before the HTTP server starts
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:615-616,707-708 — RLS_READS_ENABLED/RLS_WRITES_ENABLED are delivered from secrets into the droplet .env
docs/RLS-rollout.md:19-23 — repo-level GitHub secrets (2026-08-30) enable a broad list (~44 read modules, ~17 write modules); the live secret values are not visible from the repository
findings.impact: Postgres RLS is not the enforcement layer for any module not in the allow-list: tenant isolation still rests on middleware (requireOrgAccess + per-handler scoping). A middleware regression would therefore not be caught by the database. The startup guard only proves the list is non-empty, not that the high-risk modules are in it.
findings.recommendation: Record the deployed allow-list contents and date in docs/RLS-rollout.md (or emit it as a startup log line) so the rollout state is reviewable; extend the rollout to the remaining write paths; keep the IR-P1-006 bypass metrics and MCTTenantScopeRegression rule as the runtime backstop.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: fail-closed startup guard and metric wiring present (rls-startup-check.ts, portal_rls_bypass_total); the default remains the service-role client and the per-module rollout is operational/owner-gated — status stays partially-fixed.

findings.title: Prometheus loads rules but has no alert routing
evidence: infra/digitalocean/prometheus.yml:14-17 — alerting.alertmanagers targets alertmanager:9093
infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml:5-143 — MCTServiceDown, MCTHighRequestErrorRate, Watchdog, MCTImpersonationBurst, MCTTenantScopeRegression, MCTRlsEnforcedShareCollapsed
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:239-307 — alertmanager service renders alertmanager.tmpl.yml and starts with the rendered config
infra/digitalocean/alertmanager.tmpl.yml:63-100 — route: critical / default / watchdog; :105-152 — receivers with external webhook + Slack; :147-152 — Watchdog to the external dead-man's-switch URL
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:711-729 — production deploy fails closed when ALERTMANAGER_WATCHDOG_WEBHOOK_URL is empty
findings.impact: Resolved: firing alerts now have a delivery path and the monitoring path itself is watched off-box. Residual risk is delivery configuration (operator-provided URLs/credentials), not missing routing.
findings.recommendation: No code change required. Keep the watchdog URL + basic-auth secrets provisioned per environment and re-run the IR-P0-003 fail-closed check on every prod deploy (already enforced).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: Prometheus alerting block + Alertmanager service + watchdog receiver are all present in the as-built compose; deploy fails closed in prod without the watchdog URL. Still fixed.

findings.title: Web middleware gates routes on an unverified JWT `exp`
evidence: apps/web/middleware.ts:5-16 — comment documents the gate as best-effort, non-authoritative UX (no signature verification)
apps/web/middleware.ts:17-26 — isTokenExpired base64-decodes the payload and reads exp only
apps/web/middleware.ts:115,134-138 — unauthenticated/expired cookie redirects portal+admin routes to /login
apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts:100-134 — the API verifies the JWT signature (HS256 pinned) and exp on every call, with the Supabase fallback at :136-166
apps/web/lib/api.ts:9-20 — server components/server actions always forward the cookie token to the API, which re-checks it
findings.impact: A forged-but-unexpired cookie reaches only the page shell; no data is served from the middleware decision. Residual: the middleware is a redirect/UX control, so anyone treating it as an authz boundary would be wrong — the code comment now says so.
findings.recommendation: Keep the comment and add a unit assertion that no page or server action reads authorization state from middleware; if a true edge gate is ever wanted, verify the signature in middleware or move to a signed session cookie.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: documented as a non-authoritative UX gate (apps/web/middleware.ts:5-16, commit 6ea9cb8e); behavior intentionally unchanged because the API verifies tokens — status stays partially-fixed.

findings.title: API always enqueues to BullMQ while the worker backend is a separate setting with no parity check
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/task-producer.ts:76-104 — enqueueTask always constructs a BullMQ queue on REDIS_URL and returns true after add(); the API env schema has no QUEUE_BACKEND setting
apps/worker/src/env.ts:11,44-65 — QUEUE_BACKEND enum bullmq|sqs|inline (default inline; inline rejected when NODE_ENV=production)
apps/worker/src/consumer-sqs.ts:80-108 — the worker consumes whichever backend is configured (bullmq | sqs | inline)
apps/api/src/lib/webhook-dispatcher.ts:147-153 — when enqueueTask returns true the API returns and relies on the worker to deliver the webhook
apps/api/src/lib/notify.ts:215-221 — a queued notification email is recorded as delivered (emailQueued:true) on successful enqueue
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:138 — compose pins QUEUE_BACKEND: bullmq for the worker container only
findings.impact: If the worker's QUEUE_BACKEND (or its REDIS_URL) ever drifts from the API's implicit BullMQ/Redis coupling, the API keeps accepting tasks and reporting success while the worker consumes nothing: outbound webhooks, notification emails and scheduled scans are silently lost. No health check or alert compares the two sides.
findings.recommendation: Give the API the same QUEUE_BACKEND contract and fail closed on a producer/consumer mismatch (or derive both from one deployment value); add a startup/health assertion that a test task enqueued by the API is observed by the worker; document the coupling in the deployment docs.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d. Adjacent to RES-P2-003 (worker refuses inline in prod, verified-fixed) and RES-P3-003 (AGENTS.md queue-backend doc gap, open) but distinct: this is the API/worker producer-consumer contract, which remains unchecked.

findings.title: One non-replicated Redis backs queue, cache, idempotency and scan locks; failure degrades silently
evidence: infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:27-61 — single redis service (48m cap, no replication); the same instance serves BullMQ, response cache, idempotency keys and worker scan locks
apps/api/src/lib/task-producer.ts:97-104 — on Redis failure enqueue returns false and callers silently fall back to inline execution
apps/api/src/lib/idempotency.ts:52,107-136 — claimIdempotencyKey falls back to a per-process in-memory map
apps/worker/src/lib/idempotency.ts:10,44-52 — the worker has its own in-memory fallback map, so API and worker cannot dedupe against each other while Redis is down
apps/worker/src/lib/scan-lock.ts:43-50 — if Redis is unavailable the scheduled-scan lock is skipped ('single-replica assumed') and every replica would run the scan
apps/api/src/middleware/cache.ts:35-52 — response cache silently falls back to per-process memory
docs/PLATFORM_FAILURE_RUNBOOKS.md:60-64 — the runbook treats repeated Redis OOM as a capacity signal (48 MB cap)
findings.impact: A Redis outage silently changes delivery semantics instead of failing closed: duplicate webhook deliveries/notification emails become possible (API and worker dedupe maps are independent), idempotency claims are lost, scans run unlocked, and the cache goes cold. With more than one replica the per-process fallbacks diverge. None of these transitions is alerted.
findings.recommendation: Separate the queue from the cache (or enable Redis persistence/replication) and raise the memory cap; make idempotency degrade loudly (metric + alert) rather than silently, and document the degraded-mode semantics in the failure runbooks; add a Prometheus alert on Redis OOM/eviction and queue depth (worker_task_queue_depth is exported but has no rule).
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d. Related to the single-droplet SPOF row but a distinct failure mode (semantics change, not just availability).

findings.title: Architecture diagram and ADR 004 contradict the as-built runtime
evidence: docs/ARCHITECTURE_DIAGRAM.md:137 — deploy flow described as `docker save | gzip | ssh | gunzip | docker load`; the as-built deploy pulls digest-verified images from GHCR (.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:776-782,808-815)

docs/ARCHITECTURE_DIAGRAM.md:149 — 'In-memory cache | Acceptable for single-instance; Redis upgrade path'; the as-built cache is Redis-backed with a memory fallback (apps/api/src/middleware/cache.ts:27-60)
docs/adr/README.md:23 — ADR 004 'In-Memory Cache over Redis' is still marked Accepted
docs/ARCHITECTURE_DIAGRAM.md:3-110 — the diagram omits Prometheus/Alertmanager, the worker health port, /metrics auth and the RLS client swap
docs/PRODUCTION_VS_TESTING_DOMAINS.md:8-16,31 — still describes Vercel + AWS ALB/ECS origins, superseded by ADR 001 (DigitalOcean droplet + Caddy)
findings.impact: Operators and AI agents form a wrong mental model of the deploy path and the caching layer, and the prompt's 'diagrams match deployment reality' check fails. The ECS/Vercel doc also contradicts the current environment model.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate docs/ARCHITECTURE_DIAGRAM.md from the compose file and terraform; supersede ADR 004 with the Redis-backed cache decision; rewrite docs/PRODUCTION_VS_TESTING_DOMAINS.md for the droplet topology (overlaps INFRA-P2-005, owned by the infra domain).
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d. PRODUCTION_VS_TESTING_DOMAINS.md overlap with INFRA-P2-005 is recorded; the diagram/ADR portion is architecture-domain.

findings.title: `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` runtime override is inert for server-side code; docs claim internal SSR routing
evidence: infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:192 — web container runtime env `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL: http://api:4000`
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:333 — the web image is built with `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://<api domain>` (build arg)
apps/web/lib/env.ts:66-68 — static `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` access; Next.js inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* at build time (values frozen after `next build`), so the runtime override does not change it
docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:22 — 'server components use http://api:4000 inside Docker'; docs/ARCHITECTURE_DIAGRAM.md:116 and docs/ONBOARDING.md:74 make the same claim
apps/web/next.config.mjs:23-30 — rewrites() also captures the value at config/build time
findings.impact: Server-side SDK calls (SSR data fetches, server actions, SSE/report URLs) leave the compose network and traverse the public edge (Cloudflare -> Caddy) using the build-time public URL, despite the compose value and the docs. The compose value is misleading dead config, and an edge/DNS outage can break SSR while all containers are healthy. Confidence: medium-high (Next.js documents NEXT_PUBLIC_* as build-time inlined; not reproduced with a running build in this audit).
findings.recommendation: Read a server-only variable (e.g. API_INTERNAL_URL) at runtime for server-side code and keep NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL for the browser only; or correct the docs and remove the inert compose value. Validate by logging the resolved base URL from the running web container.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d. Validation step: `docker exec mct-portal-web-1 node -e "console.log(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL)"` is NOT sufficient (process env is set) — check the bundled server chunk or add a one-shot startup log of the URL actually used by getApiClient().

findings.title: Request timeout returns 408 but never cancels the handler
evidence: apps/api/src/middleware/request-timeout.ts:3-18 — a setTimeout writes a 408 when headers are unsent; there is no AbortController, req.destroy(), or signal threaded to downstream work
apps/api/src/app.ts:151 — requestTimeout(30000) is mounted globally after csrf
findings.impact: A slow mutation keeps executing (DB writes, queue enqueues, webhook dispatch) after the client has received a timeout; a client retry can duplicate work unless it sends an Idempotency-Key (the SDK does for unsafe requests, but other callers may not). On the 1 vCPU droplet this also wastes the request budget.
findings.recommendation: Either thread an AbortSignal into handlers and abort downstream work, or document that the 408 is advisory only and require Idempotency-Key on mutating routes; add a regression test asserting a mutation after 408 is not applied twice.

findings.title: Worker metrics/health are unauthenticated while the API gates /metrics
evidence: apps/worker/src/health-server.ts:8-56 — serves /health and /metrics on 0.0.0.0:3001 with no token; /health discloses registered task names and queue state
apps/api/src/app.ts:154-171 — API /metrics returns 404 unless METRICS_TOKEN is configured and presented as a bearer token
infra/digitalocean/prometheus.yml:33-39 — the mct-worker scrape has no authorization block (the mct-api scrape does, :22-31)
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:130-184 — the worker port is not published (compose-network access only), so exposure is limited to the droplet/compose network
findings.impact: Any process or container on the droplet can read worker internals (task names, queue health, metrics labels). No public exposure today, but the trust boundary is inconsistent with the API and would become a leak if the port were ever published or the network shared.
findings.recommendation: Gate the worker /metrics with the same METRICS_TOKEN check (or bind the metrics listener to a separate authenticated port) and add the authorization block to the Prometheus worker scrape; keep /health minimal.

# Architecture and Runtime Topology Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: `https://github.com/MaineCyberTech/mainecybertech` (read-only worktree `/tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target`)
- Branch: `main`
- Commit SHA: `8d299b8dc271c410b9ae2ceeda3d2c6c997af8fd`
- Generated at: 2026-10-11 (subagent domain pass)
- Auditor: domain subagent `02_architecture_runtime_topology` (area ARCH)
- Output path: `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8/02_architecture_runtime_topology.md`
- Scope limitations: repository-only audit. No running stack, no droplet access, no GitHub environment secrets — live-dependent rows are marked `unverified`. No build/test commands were run (resource discipline).

## Scope

Reviewed: monorepo structure; frontend/backend/worker boundaries; auth/session flow; authorization and tenant boundaries; request lifecycle; data flow; background jobs; queues; webhooks; realtime; notifications; external integrations; deployment topology; environment parity; error handling; runtime validation.

Not reviewed (other domains): RLS policy SQL correctness (37), CI/CD governance (10), supply chain (11), infra drift (12), resilience drills (13), observability rules (14), performance (15), security exploitation (06/24/25/26).

## Evidence Reviewed

Live-dependent rows: deployed RLS allow-list contents, GitHub environment secrets, actual alert delivery, and the running web container's effective API URL are `unverified` (no read-only live access authorized in this pass).

## Executive Summary

The platform is a pnpm/Turbo monorepo (`apps/api`, `apps/web`, `apps/worker`, `packages/sdk|ui|config`) deployed as a single Docker Compose stack on one DigitalOcean droplet per environment, behind Caddy + Cloudflare, with hosted Supabase as the only data store and a single Redis for queue/cache/idempotency/locks. The request path is well-layered: helmet/CORS/body-parse → security headers → sanitizer → IP + per-user rate limits → request-id/logger → idempotency → CSRF → 30s timeout → routers → notFound/error handler. Tenant scope is resolved per request (`orgScope`) and audited; a per-module RLS client swap exists with a production fail-closed boot guard. Background work is BullMQ-backed with a worker task registry, staggered scheduled scans, Redis scan locks, webhook retry + dead letters, and an SSE notification stream.

Strengths: digest-verified GHCR deploys with provenance attestation; deploy health gate with auto-revert; fail-closed production boot checks (RLS reads, Turnstile, field encryption); Prometheus + Alertmanager with an off-box watchdog; documented failure runbooks; per-module RLS rollout with runtime bypass metrics.

Major risks: (1) the topology remains a hard SPOF — host loss or a failed deploy is a full outage, and every deploy is stop-the-world; (2) the API/worker queue contract is split across two unconnected settings, so drift silently drops tasks; (3) one non-replicated Redis silently changes delivery semantics on failure; (4) architecture docs/ADRs describe a superseded runtime.

Recommended next actions: verify the producer/consumer queue contract with a health assertion; document the deployed RLS allow-list; separate queue and cache (or replicate Redis); regenerate the architecture diagram and supersede ADR 004.

| Idempotency | `lib/idempotency.ts` (API + worker) | Webhook/HTTP dedupe | Redis SET NX + per-process fallback | Med | Fallbacks don't dedupe across processes |
| Scan locks | `worker/src/lib/scan-lock.ts` | One replica runs each scan | Redis lock; unlocked fallback | Med | "single-replica assumed" |

## Detailed Review

### Item: Monorepo structure

- Evidence: `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`apps/*`, `packages/*`), `turbo.json` (build/dev/lint/test/typecheck/coverage tasks), `apps/{api,web,worker}`, `packages/{sdk,ui,config}`.
- What it does: pnpm workspace with Turbo task orchestration; apps build independently (Dockerfiles per app); `packages/sdk` is the typed API client + DB types shared by web/API/worker.
- Current controls: `pnpm-lock.yaml` frozen installs in CI; per-app Docker builds; turbo outputs cached.
- Missing controls: `packages/sdk` has `main: ./src/index.ts` (no build), so every consumer compiles it — a deliberate but undocumented coupling.
- Risks: Low.

### Item: Frontend/backend/worker boundaries

- Evidence: web calls the API through `@mct/sdk` (server: `apps/web/lib/api.ts`, browser: `lib/client-api.ts`); the worker never serves HTTP except its health server (`worker/src/health-server.ts`); the API never consumes the queue.
- What it does: browser → Caddy → web; SSR → API; async work → Redis → worker; observability internal.
- Missing controls: no runtime check that the web container's effective API URL matches the intended path (finding).
- Risks: Medium (hidden routing assumption).

### Item: Auth/session flow

- Evidence: `POST /api/v1/auth/*` issues Supabase JWTs; web sets `mct_session` (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, domain `.mainecybertech.com`) via `lib/cookie-domain.ts:14-26`; API `requireAuth` verifies HS256 with a comma-separated secret list then falls back to Supabase `getUser` with a 5s timeout (`middleware/auth.ts:100-166`); MFA step (`mfa.ts`); API-key path (`mct_*`) pins the key's org (`auth.ts:67-88`).
- Current controls: algorithm pinning, exp check, MFA gate, API-key org pinning, CSRF double-submit for cookie auth, SSE re-validation every 5 min.
- Missing controls: web middleware remains a non-authoritative exp gate (accepted, documented).
- Risks: Low.

### Item: Authorization and tenant boundaries

- Evidence: `requireOrgAccess` resolves `orgScope` (explicit query/body → active-org header/cookie → first approved membership), audits cross-tenant access (`logImpersonation`), and blocks body/query org mismatches (`assertBodyOrgMatches`); `assertOrgScopeMatches`/`assertSharesActiveOrg` for target checks; `getScopedClient` swaps to the RLS client per module allow-list; `assertRlsStartupConfig` refuses prod boot when reads are empty.
- Missing controls: no reviewable record of which modules are enabled in each environment; writes can still fall back to service-role.
- Risks: Medium.

### Item: Request lifecycle

- Evidence: `app.ts:89-151` (helmet → CORS reflect → 10MB JSON + rawBody capture → cookieParser → securityHeaders → inputSanitizer → 300/15min IP limiter with webhook skip → 600/15min user limiter → request-id/logger → idempotency → CSRF → 30s timeout) → routers → `notFoundHandler` → `errorHandler` (Sentry, generic 5xx message, `X-Request-ID`).
- Missing controls: 408 is advisory only; webhooks skip the IP limiter but are still covered by the per-user/IP limiter.
- Risks: Low-Medium.

### Item: Data flow

- Evidence: all DB access is Supabase REST with the service-role key by default (`services/supabase.ts:63-83`) through a circuit breaker + duration histogram; user-scoped client memoized per request (`:115-177`); Redis cache; audit writes retry 3× and log a gap on failure (`services/audit.ts`).
- Risks: Medium (see Redis and RLS findings).

### Item: Background jobs / queues / webhooks / realtime / notifications

- Evidence: `worker/src/main.ts` schedules 6 fixed tasks + 17 staggered module scans; `withScanLock` dedupes replicas; BullMQ job options `attempts:3` exponential backoff (`task-producer.ts:48-56`); webhook retry with DLQ (`tasks/webhook-retry.ts`); SSE stream (`routes/notifications.ts:47-173`); notification channels + dedupe key (`lib/notify.ts`, `notification-channels.ts`).
- Missing controls: task-level DLQ for non-webhook jobs; queue backend parity; worker metrics auth.
- Risks: Medium.

### Item: Deployment topology / environment parity

- Evidence: Terraform droplet (one per env, `prevent_destroy`), firewall (Cloudflare CIDRs only for 80/443; SSH allowlist required), compose stack (7 always-on services + profile-gated e2e, mem/PID limits, read-only roots, cap_drop ALL), deploy pipeline (validate → build+scan+attest → verify attestations → e2e+migrations for prod only → SSH deploy with auto-revert), Caddy prod/dev Caddyfiles, Alertmanager template with env substitution.
- Environment parity: dev and prod run the same NODE_ENV=production stack with production fail-closed checks; dev deploys skip e2e and migrations (prod gates only). Secrets are per-environment.
- Risks: Medium (stop-the-world deploys; dev/prod gate asymmetry is intentional).

## Findings

### Finding: Single-droplet, single-instance runtime is a hard SPOF (P2, partially-fixed)

- Severity: P2 · Confidence: high · Area: ARCH
- Evidence: `droplet.tf:1-20` (one droplet resource); `docker-compose.yml:68-184` (one api/worker/web), `:27-61` (one Redis), `:310-337` (one Caddy); `deploy-do.yml:809-815` (compose down before up).
- What is happening: no replication at any layer; deploys stop the stack before starting the new one.
- Why it matters: host/Redis/Caddy loss is a total outage; every deploy is an outage window.
- Recommended fix: keep runbooks; budget blue/green or at least an in-place `up -d` path; state the downtime window in `docs/SLO.md`.
- Status: partially-fixed (runbooks present, topology unchanged).

### Finding: API defaults to the service-role DB client (RLS bypass) (P2, partially-fixed)

- Severity: P2 · Confidence: high · Area: ARCH
- Evidence: `supabase.ts:198-226`; `rls-startup-check.ts:40-46`; `main.ts:12-14`; `deploy-do.yml:615-616,707-708`; `docs/RLS-rollout.md:19-23`.
- What is happening: RLS enforcement is opt-in per module; the guard only proves the list is non-empty.
- Why it matters: tenant isolation still depends on middleware for unlisted modules.
- Recommended fix: record the deployed allow-list in the runbook; extend the rollout; keep the bypass metrics/alert.
- Status: partially-fixed.

### Finding: Prometheus loads rules but has no alert routing (P2, verified-fixed)

- Severity: P2 · Confidence: high · Area: ARCH
- Evidence: `prometheus.yml:14-17`; `docker-compose.yml:239-307`; `alertmanager.tmpl.yml:63-100,105-152`; `deploy-do.yml:711-729`.
- Status: verified-fixed (no action required).

### Finding: Web middleware gates routes on an unverified JWT `exp` (P3, partially-fixed)

- Severity: P3 · Confidence: high · Area: ARCH
- Evidence: `apps/web/middleware.ts:5-16,17-26,115,134-138`; `apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts:100-134`.
- Status: partially-fixed (documented UX gate; behavior intentionally unchanged).

### Finding: API always enqueues to BullMQ while the worker backend is a separate setting with no parity check (P2, open)

- Severity: P2 · Confidence: high · Area: ARCH
- Evidence: `task-producer.ts:76-104`; `worker/src/env.ts:11,44-65`; `consumer-sqs.ts:80-108`; `webhook-dispatcher.ts:147-153`; `notify.ts:215-221`; compose `:138`.
- Why it matters: drift silently loses webhooks, emails and scheduled scans while the API reports success.
- Recommended fix: one backend contract + fail-closed parity assertion + an enqueue/consume smoke check.
- Status: open.

### Finding: One non-replicated Redis backs queue, cache, idempotency and scan locks; failure degrades silently (P2, open)

- Severity: P2 · Confidence: high · Area: ARCH
- Evidence: compose `:27-61`; `task-producer.ts:97-104`; API `idempotency.ts:52,107-136`; worker `idempotency.ts:10,44-52`; `scan-lock.ts:43-50`; `cache.ts:35-52`; `PLATFORM_FAILURE_RUNBOOKS.md:60-64`.
- Why it matters: duplicates become possible and dedup/locks are lost without any alert.
- Recommended fix: split queue vs cache or replicate; make degradation loud; alert on OOM/queue depth.
- Status: open.

### Finding: Architecture diagram and ADR 004 contradict the as-built runtime (P3, open)

- Severity: P3 · Confidence: high · Area: ARCH
- Evidence: `ARCHITECTURE_DIAGRAM.md:137,149`; `adr/README.md:23`; `deploy-do.yml:776-788`; `cache.ts:27-60`; `PRODUCTION_VS_TESTING_DOMAINS.md:8-16,31`.
- Recommended fix: regenerate the diagram; supersede ADR 004; fix the domain doc (INFRA-P2-005 overlap).
- Status: open.

### Finding: `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` runtime override is inert for server-side code (P3, open)

- Severity: P3 · Confidence: medium · Area: ARCH
- Evidence: compose `:192`; `deploy-do.yml:333`; `apps/web/lib/env.ts:66-68`; `TROUBLESHOOTING.md:22`; `ARCHITECTURE_DIAGRAM.md:116`; `ONBOARDING.md:74`.
- Why it matters: SSR traffic uses the public edge, and the docs claim otherwise; the runtime value is misleading.
- Recommended fix: server-only `API_INTERNAL_URL` read at runtime (or fix docs and remove the value).
- Status: open.

### Finding: Request timeout returns 408 but never cancels the handler (P3, open)

- Severity: P3 · Confidence: high · Area: ARCH
- Evidence: `request-timeout.ts:3-18`; `app.ts:151`.
- Recommended fix: thread an AbortSignal or document the advisory semantics + require Idempotency-Key on mutations.
- Status: open.

### Finding: Worker metrics/health are unauthenticated while the API gates /metrics (P3, open)

- Severity: P3 · Confidence: high · Area: ARCH
- Evidence: `worker/src/health-server.ts:8-56`; `app.ts:154-171`; `prometheus.yml:33-39`; compose `:130-184`.
- Recommended fix: gate worker /metrics with METRICS_TOKEN and add the scrape authorization block.
- Status: open.
